verdict.rationale: Bitwarden describes itself as an 'open source password manager', and community comments confirm it relicensed back to a free/open license after the SDK controversy. The only concrete license evidence is for a first-party component, the GPL-3.0 MCP server repo. That controversy was resolved, so it is not a dispute. Missing for 10: first-party documentation linking the main client and server source repositories with their licenses, explicit confirmation that the SDK and clients are now under an OSI-approved license, and hands-on verification of reading the core product source.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The most trusted open source password manager for passwords, passkeys, and secrets
First-party repo (bitwarden/mcp-server, GPL-3.0), published to npm.
Thank you to Bitwarden for relicensing back to Free/Open License
